The bug is fixed: `![x\"x](x)` with `-x smarty` now gives `

`, the same as the unescaped input. The new tests pass, and the full suite has the same 8 failures it had before my change. **Cause:** a backslash escape like `\"` is held as a placeholder while the document is processed. The step that turns the placeholder back into `"` ran *after* the HTML was written out, so the character never got HTML-escaped. That made the quote end up raw inside `alt=""`. Any escapable character in any attribute was affected, not just quotes with smarty. For example, `attr_list` with `title="a\"b"` produced `title="a"b"`. **Fix:** I moved that step to just before the HTML is written, so the normal output escaping sees the real characters. - `markdown/treeprocessors.py`: new `UnescapeTreeprocessor`, which restores escaped characters in element text and attributes. It's registered as `'unescape'` and runs last. - `markdown/postprocessors.py`: the old `UnescapePostprocessor` no longer runs by default. The class is still there but warns that it's deprecated, so third-party code that uses it keeps working. - `markdown/inlinepatterns.py`: raw inline HTML is passed through untouched and never gets escaped, so it now restores the escaped characters itself as it's stored. Output is unchanged; for example, `` still comes out as written. - `markdown/extensions/toc.py`: now uses the new class. **Visible output change:** a backslash-escaped `>` in text now renders as `>` instead of a bare `>`. Browsers display both the same. I updated `tests/basic/backlash-escapes.html` to match, since that was the only existing test that changed. **Tests:** - New `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py` covers escaped quotes with smarty in text, image alt/title, link href/title, and `attr_list` values. The four attribute tests fail on the original code. - `tests/test_syntax/inline/test_images.py`: two tests for escaped characters in `alt` without smarty. Both fail on the original code. - `tests/test_apis.py`: checks that the old postprocessor warns but still works. I also updated `docs/extensions/api.md` and the 3.4 release notes. **About the test run:** - `pytest tests` stops before running anything because pytest can't collect the `TestSuite` class in `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_md_in_html.py`. That happens on the original code too. - I ran the whole suite with `unittest discover` instead. The 8 failures are the same before and after my change: raw-HTML/comment tests in `test_html_blocks` and `test_md_in_html`, which I think come from differences in Python 3.12's HTML parser. - flake8 isn't installed in the venv, so I didn't lint. Nothing is committed.
